title: One lame duck and two turkeys as Trump plays the hits at Thanksgiving ceremony
summary:
Levity was in short supply as president, reeling from midterms rout, talked up his achievements – and fixated on White House vanity project

For some, it was his pardoning of the January 6…

blocks.text: For some, it was his pardoning of the January 6 rioters or the deployment of masked ICE agents. For others, it was Elon Musk’s chainsaw or the demolition of the White House East Wing.
Donald Trump’s second term as US president has been full of moments when people exclaim: this is the last straw! But on Tuesday even he went too far.

The Thanksgiving turkey pardoning ceremony is typically an occasion for levity with dad jokes, bad puns and bipartisan spirit, a rare glimpse of presidential self-awareness and humility. In 2010 Barack Obama, reeling from Democrats’ disastrous midterm elections, quipped: “It feels pretty good to stop at least one shellacking this November.”

But Trump, still reeling from his own midterm rout, did none of these things. Perhaps he was still scarred by his humiliatingly unfunny turn at the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner. It was just Trump being Trump, bragging about his heroic achievements and rhapsodising about his architectural overall of the White House.

Under a clear blue sky, guests were seated on his new circular granite helipad on the south lawn. The president offered by way of explanation: “It’ll be here for hopefully hundreds of years, and it’s supposed to land helicopters: it’s as good as you can get, but we use it for other things too. We just realised it’s locationally perfect.”

blocks.caption: One of the turkeys at the ceremony on Tuesday. Photograph: Matt Kaminsky/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock

blocks.text: Wearing dark coat, white shirt and cream tie, the master builder welcomed guests and claimed the White House had “never looked better than it’s looked right now”. Then a delightful thought suddenly came to him. “Do you mind if I turn around and look?”

The president rotated and gazed at the north face of the White House, bedecked with seasonal wreaths. He complained: “I was criticised for fixing it up and making it look beautiful, fixing broken windows, fixing broken moldings, and it was a mess, and now it’s beautiful. Now it’s the way it should be. It is the symbol of our country and I think spending 10 minutes a day on it was very worthwhile.”
Ten minutes a day? A generous estimate from a decorator-in-chief who was once reportedly found supergluing gold appliqués to the Oval Office fireplace.

Trump proceeded to run through a guest list that included outgoing House speaker Mike Johnson, treasury secretary Scott Bessent (“central casting”), defense secretary Pete Hegseth (“who’s been fantastic”) and attorney general Todd Blanche (“Todd has been very busy”).

When he came to the farmers from West Virginia who had provided this year’s turkeys, named Freedom and Feathers, he could not resist observing: “We won West Virginia by 45 points. At least, I did when I was on the ballot. I don’t know what happened. I won it by a lot. I don’t know what the hell happened with this last election. Somebody please explain it to me.”

As in past years, the turkeys had stayed overnight at the nearby Willard Hotel. But that tradition too is coming to an end, Trump said. “I’m pleased to announce that next year we’ll be able to have a special location right over there in that rather small ballroom being built. It’s going to host a lot of people and a couple of turkeys next year.”

blocks.caption: Trump pardoned the turkeys named Freedom and Feathers. Photograph: Evelyn Hockstein/Reuters

blocks.text: Ah, his favourite subject. There it was for all to see: a giant structure of concrete and steel, dwarfing construction workers in helmets, overalls and yellow vests amid a clang of hammers on pipes. Trump, the property wheeler-dealer from New York, has made clear over the past two years that this vanity project is what he really cares about.

He sounded like Emperor Palpatine or Darth Vader boasting about his new and seemingly indestructible Death Star: “It’s a ballroom military complex, and it’s going to be one of the – probably I would say it’s as strong a building, and I don’t want to go totally crazy here because I’ll be criticised by the fake news, but it’s, I would say that it is the strongest building ever built in this country.

“That’s a big statement. It is a very strong building. They say missile-proof, drone-proof, bulletproof, and everything else, and but it’s going to be also one of the most beautiful ballrooms, I think the most beautiful ballroom ever built, and it’s going to be representative likewise with our country, and you see the way it fits so nicely.”

The president then delved into a long and meandering rally-style speech along the lines of “you’ve never had it so good”. The past two years have been “amazing” and “incredible”. The stock market has gained $25tn in wealth, he claimed, only to lose $6tn because of the midterm election result.

But Trump is in a forgiving mood. He just got Jensen Huang reinstated at Nvidia despite an alleged affair with a Chinese spy. Now he placed his hand on Freedom’s back and uttered, “Congratulations” – ensuring that both it and Feathers will live out their days at Texas A+M University. Trump might be a lame duck but he still has power to pardon a turkey or two.
